description: Support for Stored Procedures - Add the ability to execute stored procedures with input parameters, output parameters, and return values. Provide both sync and async APIs integrated with the existing SqlClient and AsyncSqlClient.
steps: Create DBTools/Abstractions/IStoredProcedureClient.cs with interfaces: IStoredProcedureClient (sync) with methods ExecuteStoredProcedure(string procedureName, StoredProcedureParameter[] parameters) returning StoredProcedureResult, and ExecuteStoredProcedureReader(string procedureName, StoredProcedureParameter[] parameters) returning DataTable. Also IAsyncStoredProcedureClient (async) with ExecuteStoredProcedureAsync and ExecuteStoredProcedureReaderAsync (with CancellationToken).

Create DBTools/StoredProcedures/StoredProcedureParameter.cs with a class containing: Name (string), Value (object), Direction (ParameterDirection from System.Data - Input, Output, InputOutput, ReturnValue), DbType (System.Data.DbType, optional/nullable), Size (int?, optional for output params).
Create DBTools/StoredProcedures/StoredProcedureResult.cs with a class containing: ReturnValue (object), OutputParameters (Dictionary<string, object>), RowsAffected (int).

Create DBTools/StoredProcedures/StoredProcedureClient.cs implementing IStoredProcedureClient: takes IDbProvider, connectionString in constructor. ExecuteStoredProcedure creates a DbCommand with CommandType = CommandType.StoredProcedure, adds parameters respecting Direction, executes via ExecuteNonQuery, then reads back output/return values. ExecuteStoredProcedureReader does the same but uses ExecuteReader and loads into DataTable.
Create DBTools/StoredProcedures/AsyncStoredProcedureClient.cs implementing IAsyncStoredProcedureClient: async versions of the same operations using ExecuteNonQueryAsync and ExecuteReaderAsync.
Register IStoredProcedureClient and IAsyncStoredProcedureClient in ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddDbTools() as scoped services.
Create DBToolsUnitTest/StoredProcedures/StoredProcedureParameterTests.cs testing parameter construction with various directions.

Create DBToolsUnitTest/StoredProcedures/StoredProcedureClientTests.cs testing that the client correctly configures DbCommand with CommandType.StoredProcedure, adds parameters with correct directions (using SqlServerProvider which creates real SqlCommand objects for inspection).
acceptance_criteria: StoredProcedureParameter supports Input, Output, InputOutput, and ReturnValue directions
StoredProcedureResult captures return value, output parameters, and rows affected
StoredProcedureClient and AsyncStoredProcedureClient are fully implemented
DI registration is added to ServiceCollectionExtensions
Unit tests verify parameter setup, command configuration (CommandType.StoredProcedure), and result object construction
verification: Verify interfaces follow existing pattern (XML docs, namespace consistency)
Verify implementations use IDbProvider.CreateConnection/CreateCommand pattern consistent with AsyncSqlClient
Verify DI registration follows existing scoped pattern
Verify tests use MSTest attributes and TestBase
